title: Pasta with Cream Sauce and Seafood

content.title: About
content.content: Pasta with cream sauce and seafood is an Italian-inspired dish that combines al dente pasta, a silky cream sauce, and a mix of seafood such as shrimp, mussels, and calamari. The sauce is made from cream, white wine, garlic, and herbs, while the seafood is quickly sautéed to stay tender. The dish provides high‑quality protein, omega‑3 fatty acids, and B‑vitamins.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The creamy sauce is often called “Alfredo” in the U.S., though the original Italian version differs.
Seafood is added at the end of cooking to prevent it from becoming rubbery.
Cream stabilizes aromatic compounds, giving the sauce a rounded flavor.
Traditionally the dish is finished with grated Parmesan, enhancing umami.
It is especially popular in coastal restaurants where fresh seafood is available daily.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Seafood such as shrimp and mussels provides high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Seafood supplies EPA and DHA, which support heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Calcium and vitamin D
items.content: Cream and some seafood (e.g., mussels) contribute calcium and vitamin D for strong bones.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish contains B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Garlic and white wine add polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp, mussels, or calamari.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The cream sauce is rich in saturated fat and calories, so portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑watching diets.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Prepared sauces and seafood are often salted; people with hypertension should limit added salt.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: Improperly stored seafood can harbor bacteria; it should be cooked and kept at proper temperatures.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cook the pasta until al dente, reserve a cup of cooking water, then drain. Sauté the seafood in olive oil, add garlic, wine, and cream, and simmer until thickened. Toss the pasta with the sauce, adding a splash of the reserved water if needed. Top with grated Parmesan and fresh parsley, serve hot, and finish with a squeeze of lemon if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat gently, adding a little water or cream to restore sauce consistency. Freezing is not recommended, as the cream sauce may separate.
